Hand-painted stylized game texture in a soft painterly style like a modern anime-inspired 3D RPG. Strictly orthographic top-down view, flat even diffuse lighting with no directional shadows and no cast shadows at all (the carving reads by soft painted value only), no perspective, no horizon. Subject: a huge round stone clock dial carved into the floor of an abandoned cloister, seen from directly above, the circle filling the square frame edge to edge, centred. Concentric carved stone rings in cool blue-grey and lavender-grey stone with fine hairline cracks and a little pale moss in the joints; an outer ring of sixty small engraved minute ticks; a wide ring with twelve large engraved roman-numeral hour marks (XII exactly at the top, III at the right, VI at the bottom, IX at the left), the grooves inlaid with faint pale silver; between the rings a thin engraved band of simple geometric ornament; a smaller inner ring of radial flagstones; a plain round stone boss at the centre. No clock hands. Corners outside the circle: plain dark slate flagstones. No text other than the numerals, no border, no frame, no objects on it.
